literal: Suffering having experienced, unable to bear, wept tears indeed, wealth wearing away weapon.
translation: The tears shed by subjects who suffer and cannot bear the cruelty of a tyrant are indeed the weapon that wears away his wealth.
modern: கொடுங்கோன்மையால் துன்பப்பட்டு, அதனைப் பொறுக்க முடியாமல் அழுத மக்களின் கண்ணீர்தான், ஒரு மன்னனின் செல்வத்தை அழிக்கும் ஆயுதமாகும்.
explanation: This couplet warns of the silent but destructive power of the tears of oppressed subjects. When people suffer under a tyrant and find their misery unbearable ('ஆற்றாது'), they weep in despair. The tears ('கண்ணீர்') they shed are not merely signs of grief; they act as a powerful weapon ('படை') that gradually erodes and destroys the ruler's prosperity and power ('செல்வத்தைத் தேய்க்கும்'). The word 'அன்றே' emphasizes that this destruction is certain and inevitable, showing that a ruler's oppression contains the very seeds of his own ruin.
